**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 9(b) gives us a real, express vendor warranty package that meets or beats the preferred position on the material terms:

- **Conformance/performance:** "the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards" (p0034) and services "shall comply with the terms of this Agreement and shall be free from errors that materially affect their utility" (p0038).
- **Duration:** unlimited/ongoing for the Term — better than the preferred 12-month (software) / 90-day (services) windows.
- **No malicious code:** p0036 (viruses, Trojan Horses, worms, back doors, etc.).
- **Compliance with laws:** p0041 ("throughout the Term shall comply with all applicable Laws").
- **Disclaimer does not swallow it:** § 13 opens "Except as expressly set forth herein" and excepts "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement," so the "as is" language reaches only implied warranties — not walk-away territory.

Noted but not flagged: the clause lacks the preferred "professional and workmanlike" formulation and an express repair/replace/refund remedy sentence. These are sub-elements rather than material failures here, because no provision makes any remedy exclusive — we keep damages, indemnification for Kubient's breach of any warranty (p0051), and termination for uncured material breach (p0016), which is at least as favorable to us as an at-Vendor's-option repair/replace/refund. Inserting the model remedy sentence could in fact narrow our recourse, so we leave it alone.
